title: Customer IaC adaptation patterns for VPC deployments (overlays, parameter schemas, upgrade fences)
creator: Aisha Bhatia
description:
Problem statement: Customers installing Redwood Private in their VPCs need a predictable, auditable, and upgrade-safe way to customize terraform configuration without forking core modules. Current patterns are ad-hoc (per-customer forks, manual patches) which increases maintenance cost and blocks safe upgrades.

Goal: Deliver a standard set of IaC adaptation patterns that let customers express VPC-specific customizations using: overlay layers, parameter schema gating, composition-friendly modules, and upgrade fences (migrations + health checks). The outcome should reduce per-customer patching while making upgrades (module or runtime) low-risk and automatable.

Deliverables:
- Pattern catalog doc outlining 4 recommended approaches: 1) parameterized module composition, 2) overlay tfvars + patch modules, 3) hookable extension modules, 4) thin provider wrapper for customer-supplied VPCs.
- Reference terraform module layout and a sample customer overlay repo (examples/customer-acme) showing both managed-VPC and customer-VPC flows.
- Upgrade safety checklist and a small "upgrade fence" tooling rulebook (preflight checks, plan verification, canary apply, health gate).
- Health-check module (Terraform + small Python lambda) that creates probes and SLO alerts to gate rollouts.
- Migration playbook for schema changes (variable renames, resource renames) including automated plan diffs and rollback triggers.

Design decisions and patterns (high level):
1) Layered overlays: keep core modules immutable in git tags. Customers provide a thin overlay repo that references core modules by tag and adds a top-level 'overrides.tf' which only contains a small set of allowed patch operations (locals + module inputs). This avoids forks and keeps a clear upgrade path. Example: module "redwood_vpc" { source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//vpc?ref=v1.4.0" }

2) Strong parameter schema and validation: introduce a variables schema (yaml/json) and a preflight validator (go binary or python) that runs before apply. Validator enforces types, value ranges, and mutually-exclusive flags (e.g., customer_vpc_id XOR create_managed_vpc). The validator emits structured errors that CI can fail on.

3) Patch modules and composition: support small 'patch' modules hosted in the overlay repo that the root module conditionally calls. Patch modules should be thin and idempotent (output only diffs). Encourage using module composition over resource replacements. Avoid resource-level replacements unless absolutely necessary.

4) Upgrade fences and canaries: upgrades to core modules must be rolled via a canary tenant first. Provide a CI blueprint that: (a) runs `terraform plan` against canary overlay, (b) runs plan sanity checks (no >N resource replacements, no unexpected subnet changes), (c) applies to canary, (d) runs health checks for 30 minutes, (e) promotes to batch of 5 tenants. If health checks fail, automated rollback (terraform apply from last known-good state) is triggered.

5) Health checks and observability: shipping a small health-check terraform module that creates namespace-level endpoints and CloudWatch/Prometheus checks depending on deployment. Health-checks include runtime readiness, KV cache latency, GPU node temperature, and control-plane API liveness. Health-check results are available in Console rollout UI to gate canary promotions.

Compatibility considerations: support both (A) customer-managed VPCs with existing infra and (B) Redwood-managed VPC creation. For (A) require a minimal set of inputs (vpc_id, subnet_ids, route_table_ids) and validate them via preflight. For (B) expose opinionated defaults but allow override through variables and patch modules.

Security & compliance: preflight validator will also verify IAM roles created by overlays adhere to a least-privilege pattern and flag risky principals. The upgrade playbook requires a signed approval step for tenants with "high" data classification.

Acceptance criteria:
- Publish pattern catalog and example overlay repo under infra/examples/customer-overlay by 2025-03-15.
- Provide a working canary pipeline template in GitHub Actions and Jenkins to exercise upgrade fences.
- Create health-check terraform module and wire it into Console rollout UI (expose a small endpoint that Console can poll).
- Run 2 pilot upgrades with SRE and 3 pilot customers and capture lessons.

Risks and open questions:
- How to handle heavy customizations (customers that modify module internals)? Proposed mitigation: required onboarding step where Solutions Engineering converts those to patch modules and schedules a dedicated migration.
- Terraform state backfills and drift: we must define a drift detection window and plan thresholds; exact thresholds to be confirmed with SRE.
- Locking provider versions vs allowing backend improvements: we will pin module tags but allow runtime to upgrade internal provider versions via an opt-in release channel.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (internal): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/12345678/Customer+IaC+Adaptation+Patterns
- Reference modules: git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//vpc
- Example overlay repo (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/customer-examples/tree/overlay-samples/customer-acme
- Draft PR (infra): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123

Notes on implementation: start with one canonical overlay pattern and a validator binary in tools/preflight. Keep the Terraform surface stable (inputs backwards compatible) for at least two minor releases where feasible. The tooling will emit a single JSON metadata file after plan that the rollout pipeline can consume (fields: changed_resources_count, replaced_resources_count, plan_hash, drift_score).

Developer hints (snippet):
- Example variables check (pseudo):
  locals {
    has_customer_vpc = length(var.customer_vpc_id) > 0 ? true : false
  }
  resource "null_resource" "validate" {
    provisioner "local-exec" {
      command = "python ../tools/preflight/validate_overlay.py --schema overlay_schema.yaml --vars ${path.module}/terraform.tfvars"
    }
    triggers = { overlay_checksum = filemd5("${path.module}/terraform.tfvars") }
  }

Implementation milestones:
- Week 1: finalize pattern catalog and validator API contract.
- Week 2: implement preflight validator and sample overlay.
- Week 3: health-check module + pipeline gating integration.
- Week 4: pilot upgrades and doc finalization.
